Shopify Store Redesign: When to Rebuild, Fix and What to Keep

By Marie Glow StudioUpdated September 23, 2026

A redesign feels like a fresh start, and that is exactly the risk. A store that already has products, reviews, links and a search footprint has value that a careless rebuild can throw away. A good Shopify store redesign changes what is holding the store back and keeps what is working.

This guide helps you decide whether to redesign at all, what to protect, how to scope the work and how to handle redirects and SEO. It builds on 10 signs your website needs a redesign and is your website costing you customers, so read those first if you are still deciding whether something is wrong.

Redesign or fix: a quick sorting test

Write down what is bothering you, then sort each item into one of two piles.

Usually a fix

  • A confusing menu or collection order.
  • Weak product descriptions or thin photos on a few items.
  • A missing policy page or a buried contact link.
  • One page that loads slowly because of oversized images.

Usually a redesign

  • The brand has changed and the store no longer looks like it.
  • The theme cannot be adapted to the layout you need.
  • The mobile experience is poor across the whole store, not one page.
  • Fixing one thing keeps breaking another because everything was patched together.

If most of your list is in the first pile, fix first. It is cheaper, faster and carries less risk. The Shopify store optimization checklist is a good place to start.

What to keep

Before any design work, inventory what already works and decide to protect it.

  • Products and their content. Titles, descriptions and images that already sell should carry over, even if they are reformatted.
  • URLs. Product, collection and page addresses that people have bookmarked, linked to or found through search should stay the same wherever you can.
  • Reviews. Keep them attached to the products they belong to.
  • Pinterest and social links. Pins point to your URLs. Changing addresses without a plan can leave pins going to error pages.
  • Your best pages. Note which pages get visitors today and treat them with extra care.

A redesign scoping checklist

Work through this list and write an answer to each line. It keeps the project from expanding halfway through.

  1. What is the goal of the redesign, in one sentence?
  2. Which pages are in scope: homepage, collections, product template, about, contact, policies?
  3. How many products and collections will move over, and will their structure change?
  4. Is the visual identity staying or being refreshed? Do you already have a logo, colors and fonts?
  5. Who is supplying new photos and copy, and by when?
  6. Which apps or features in the current store must still work?
  7. Which URLs will change, and how will old ones be redirected?
  8. Who tests the store on phone and desktop before it goes live?
  9. When is a quiet period to launch, away from your busiest selling days?

Redirects and SEO care

Search engines and Pinterest have learned your current addresses. If an address changes, an old link should lead to the new page rather than an error. Make a list of every URL that changes, map each to its replacement and set up redirects in your Shopify admin at launch. Keep page titles and headings that already perform, and avoid deleting content just because it is old. After launch, check that the important pages open correctly and that pins and links still land where they should. For the ongoing side, see Shopify SEO for small businesses. Even a careful redesign cannot promise a particular ranking or sales result. It reduces avoidable losses and gives the store a better foundation.

If the reason for the redesign is that your brand has outgrown the store, the brand identity guide explains why the identity work should come first.

Frequently asked questions

How do I know if I need a Shopify store redesign or just fixes?

If your problems are isolated, such as a confusing menu, weak descriptions or one slow page, fixing them is usually cheaper and safer. A redesign makes sense when the brand has changed, the theme cannot support the layout you need or the mobile experience is poor across the whole store.

What should I keep when redesigning a Shopify store?

Keep the products and their content that already sell, your existing URLs wherever possible, customer reviews and any Pinterest or social links pointing to your pages. List your best performing pages before design starts and protect them.

Can a Shopify redesign hurt my SEO?

It can if URLs change without redirects or useful content is deleted. Mapping every changed address to its replacement, setting up redirects at launch and keeping strong titles and headings reduces the risk, though no redesign can promise a specific ranking.

How should I scope a Shopify store redesign?

Write down the goal, the pages in scope, how many products and collections move, whether the identity is changing, who supplies photos and copy, which features must keep working, which URLs change and who tests before launch. Answering these before design starts prevents the project growing halfway through.
